newsitem.title: CANADA: Cut unemployment premia - Canada's Conservatives.
newsitem.headline: Cut unemployment premia - Canada's Conservatives.

text.p: The leader of Canada's Conservative Party, Jean Charest, challenged the federal government on Monday to cut unemployment insurance premia by enough to halve the huge surplus in the insurance fund.

Charest told a news conference at the start of Parliament's autumn session that the fund -- formally named Employment Insurance Fund -- should generate a surplus of C$5.5 billion this year and another C$5.3 billion in 1997.

"That surplus is nothing more than a C$10 billion tax on jobs," said Charest, leader of the party that in 1993 was reduced from a governing majority to a mere two seats in the House of Commons, Parliament's elected chamber.

He proposed that Liberal Finance Minister Paul Martin lower the employment insurance premia immediately so that the surplus be cut in half by the end of 1997 and thereby put C$5 billion directly back into the Canadian economy.

A national Conservative policy convention in August pledged to push for a 10 to 20 percent income tax cut, but Martin has said Charest should show where spending cuts would come from to match proposed tax reductions.
Charest said Martin should admit that he has been counting the surplus in the employment insurance fund against the deficit to reduce its reported size.
